title: Repeated macrosteps over a unary segment
statement: Let $W$ be a finite binary Turing machine, let $a,R,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be an input word over the schedule alphabet, and let $\mathrm{base}$ be a schedule-machine configuration on $x$. Suppose its guide tape is the fixed guide of radius $R$ and, for every natural $j<B$, its unary tape contains a unit marker at coordinate $j+1$. Then for every natural $j\le B$, starting in the macrostep-check phase with unary head at $1$ and guide head at $0$, after $j(6R+8)$ steps the machine is in the macrostep-check phase with unary head at $j+1$ and guide head at $0$.
hypotheses_covered: $W$ is a finite binary Turing machine
$x$ is an input word over the schedule alphabet
the base guide tape is the fixed guide of radius $R$
for every natural $j<B$, the unary tape contains a unit marker at coordinate $j+1
the conclusion holds for every natural $j\le B$
replaced:
Suppose the base's guide tape is the fixed guide of radius $R$ and its unary tape
holds unit markers at all coordinates $1, 2, \dots, B$.  Then for every $j \le B$,
running the schedule controller for $j\,(6R + 8)$ steps from the counter-test phase
with unary head at $1$ and guide head at the origin reaches the counter-test phase
with unary head at $j + 1$ and guide head at the origin, regardless of all simulated
data and of source halting behavior.
